items.title: 66096_Monk Montgomery oral history interview
items.q: So I went and met with Garrett Asif.

ctx.x: Yeah. He said, 'Don't get excited. You don't have to sell me.' He said, 'I see it in your face. I know about your track record. I'm in agreement with you, but that's not the way it's done. It's not the way it's done.' He said, 'Now, what I'd suggest is this. I will give you an attempt, and try and work with you. I can't go to the hotel and convince them that you have this room to bring jazz into, and so-and-so, but I've got a young man that I work with on certain things. We'll have you to four-wall the place, I…

But what did I know? All I knew was like I was a bull in a china closet. Garrett Asif (?), who is a big promoter now in rock and all that sort of thing, that was the one I was going to talk to, to get it on. So I went and met with Garrett Asif. Garry wasn't into jazz but he was into promoting, and making money. And lo and behold, the old man died, heart attack. He

passed away.

That was my first hope and it looked like everything went down with him because he was a nice man, to receive me the way he did. And he understood what I was trying to say. He had a capacity for the music.
